facts.fact: On 13 October 2025 the Minister of Communication installed the ad hoc committee (created by order of 13 December 2024) to draft the national universal access strategy and action plan, so the universal access fund can bring electronic communication services to rural localities still without connectivity.

The World Bank-financed Niger Smart Villages for rural growth and digital inclusion project (P167543), run with the government, aims to increase access to cellphone and broadband services in rural areas, with closing date 23 October 2026.
facts.system: Smart Villages for rural growth and digital inclusion (P167543)

facts.fact: The World Bank report says the Smart Villages project had provided mobile broadband to 780 villages previously without coverage as of 6 August 2025, 35.86 per cent of 2,175 planned.

facts.fact: The communications minister installed an ad hoc committee on 13 October 2025 to draft a universal-access strategy and action plan to bring services to rural localities without connectivity, and the World Bank-financed PVI project (USD 100 million, 2020-2026) aims to connect 1.9 million rural people with 3G/4G coverage of 2,175 localities, slowed in 2024.

The coordinator of Niger's Projet Villages Intelligents (PVI), financed by the State and World Bank/IDA, says 3G/4G coverage has reached 657 of 2,175 rural localities in the 8 regions, with a target of 1,400 by end 2025 (the stated date of 31/12/2025 is as given).
